title: Initial wind groups did not explain the deficit of joint large NHC track and intensity errors in the Atlantic in 2019-2025
abstract: We tested whether storm-strength mixture explains a reported deficit of joint large track and absolute intensity errors in official NHC forecasts. We reused the same 2019-2025 snapshots, so this is an attribution test, not independent confirmation. In 1,605 Atlantic 48-hour cycles, joint errors above past-five-year 80th percentiles occurred in 1.184%, against 1.975% under independence within years. An exact separation by four initial best-track wind groups gave -0.787 percentage points within groups and -0.004 between groups. The within term had 95% storm limits of -1.412 to -0.064 and year limits of -1.282 to -0.218 points, with thresholds fixed. Initial strength groups therefore explained less than 1% of the measured deficit. Adding latitude left an uncertain residual of -0.501 points. An exploratory subset with nine recorded actual positions more than 200 km from land kept a deficit, but cannot exclude forecast land interaction. Earlier years, other leads and the East Pacific did not give a stable pattern. This rules out one simple mixture explanation in a specific sample. It does not identify a physical cause or test issued joint probabilities. Sparse joint events, revised data, stage exclusions, coarse strata, fixed thresholds and multiple comparisons limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes, an arithmetic check and a figure are supplied; external records stay outside the package.

display.caption: Exact separation of the recent 48-hour large-error association into terms within and between initial wind groups. Points are percentage-point differences from an independent reference within test years. Bars are 95% whole-storm bootstrap intervals with training thresholds fixed. This is a retrospective attribution test on the same source sample as the prior joint-error study.
